subject.title: feat(workspace): lint and auto-fix code fences in markdown at write time

question: Should OpenClaw add Markdown code-fence hygiene to workspace file writes, and if so should it be default auto-fix, warn/doctor-only, opt-in, or outside the core write path?
rationale: The request changes write-time semantics for user-authored Markdown and adds config/API surface, so automation should not choose the permanent product policy.

options.title: Design Opt-In Or Warn First
options.body: Keep the issue open for a parser-backed opt-in, warn-only, or doctor-lint design that avoids silent default rewrites until maintainers approve the behavior.

options.title: Approve Default Auto-Fix
options.body: Allow a future PR to mutate workspace Markdown by default with explicit config docs, skip API, upgrade proof, and broad parser tests.

options.title: Reject Core Write-Time Mutation
options.body: Close or redirect the idea toward doctor linting, docs tooling, skill guidance, or a plugin/workflow outside core file writes.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Or Warn First
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open for a parser-backed opt-in, warn-only, or doctor-lint design that avoids silent default rewrites until maintainers approve the behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current routing candidate from recent source history across agent file writes, protocol shape, and shared Markdown helpers.
